Reported longitudinal Cox models (Supplementary Tables 10-11): section 3.6,
with follow-up from the age of the last measurement used to estimate the slope
and intercept (delayed entry). Sections 3.3-3.5 start follow-up at the first
measurement (the previous version). Sensitivity analyses: 3.7 (drop-one),
3.8 (person-mean centering), 3.9 (slope scaling); Supplementary Figs. 29-30: 3.10.

Input data: AMORIS (longitudinal) from Calculating_BA_L.rmd

# 1.0 Preparing

## 1.1 Selection for longitudinal set
```{r}
# Paths, output locations and analysis parameters come from config.R in the
# repository root. Nothing below hardcodes a location.
source(here::here("config.R"))

# Count rows per sampleID
id_counts <- table(to1po2$sampleID)

# Keep only IDs with at least 3 rows
keep_ids <- names(id_counts[id_counts >= 3])

# Subset to create results_df
results_dt <- to1po2[to1po2$sampleID %in% keep_ids, ]
```

new - to answer the reviewer comment
```{r}
## 1.1b Sensitivity check: mortality in excluded (<3 measurements) vs included (>=3) groups

# Count rows per sampleID (same as your existing step)
id_counts <- table(to1po2$sampleID)

# Per-individual summary from the FULL repeat-measurement pool (to1po2),
# before restricting to >=3 measurements
ind_summary <- to1po2 %>%
  group_by(sampleID) %>%
  summarise(
    n_measurements = n(),
    age_first_meas = min(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_last_meas  = max(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    FODDATn        = first(FODDATn),
    DODSDATn       = first(DODSDATn),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    died         = !is.na(DODSDATn),
    age_at_death = as.numeric(DODSDATn - FODDATn) / 365.25,
    included     = n_measurements >= 3
  )

# Overall comparison: mortality rate in excluded (<3) vs included (>=3)
mortality_comparison <- ind_summary %>%
  group_by(included) %>%
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    n_died   = sum(died),
    pct_died = round(mean(died) * 100, 1)
  )

print(mortality_comparison)

# Among the excluded (<3 measurements) group who died, how soon after
# their LAST available measurement did death occur?
# A short gap is more consistent with "died before they could reach a 3rd test"
excluded_deaths <- ind_summary %>%
  filter(!included, died) %>%
  mutate(years_last_meas_to_death = age_at_death - age_last_meas)

summary(excluded_deaths$years_last_meas_to_death)

cat("Individuals with <3 measurements (excluded):        ", sum(!ind_summary$included), "\n")
cat("  of those, died during follow-up:                  ", sum(!ind_summary$included & ind_summary$died), "\n")
cat("Individuals with >=3 measurements (included):       ", sum(ind_summary$included), "\n")
cat("  of those, died during follow-up:                  ", sum(ind_summary$included & ind_summary$died), "\n")
```

## 1.2 Scaling
```{r}
# Define the BioAge variables you standardized
bioage_vars <- c("kdm", "kdm_advance", "phenoage", "phenoage_advance")

# Compute SDs (in years) for each
bioage_sds <- sapply(results_dt[bioage_vars], sd, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create a readable data frame
bioage_scale_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(bioage_sds),
  SD_in_years = round(bioage_sds, 2)
)

# Print the result
print(bioage_scale_df)
```

```{r}
write.table(as.data.frame(bioage_scale_df), out_path("bioage_scale_df_table_RMA.csv"), sep = ";",
```

## 1.3 Harmonize variables
```{r}
#According to SveDem
o_amoris$S_ADRD <- ifelse(o_amoris$sampleID %in% SveDem$Id & SveDem$DIAGNOSIS_BR[match(o_amoris$sampleID, SveDem$Id)] %in% c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9), 1, 0) #1-9
o_amoris$S_e_alz <- ifelse(o_amoris$sampleID %in% SveDem$Id & SveDem$DIAGNOSIS_BR[match(o_amoris$sampleID, SveDem$Id)] == 1, 1, 0) #1
o_amoris$S_l_alz <- ifelse(o_amoris$sampleID %in% SveDem$Id & SveDem$DIAGNOSIS_BR[match(o_amoris$sampleID, SveDem$Id)] == 2, 1, 0) #2
o_amoris$S_alz_vas <- ifelse(o_amoris$sampleID %in% SveDem$Id & SveDem$DIAGNOSIS_BR[match(o_amoris$sampleID, SveDem$Id)] == 3, 1, 0) #3
o_amoris$S_vas <- ifelse(o_amoris$sampleID %in% SveDem$Id & SveDem$DIAGNOSIS_BR[match(o_amoris$sampleID, SveDem$Id)] == 4, 1, 0) #4
o_amoris$S_lew <- ifelse(o_amoris$sampleID %in% SveDem$Id & SveDem$DIAGNOSIS_BR[match(o_amoris$sampleID, SveDem$Id)] == 5, 1, 0) #5
o_amoris$S_fro <- ifelse(o_amoris$sampleID %in% SveDem$Id & SveDem$DIAGNOSIS_BR[match(o_amoris$sampleID, SveDem$Id)] == 6, 1, 0) #6
o_amoris$S_par <- ifelse(o_amoris$sampleID %in% SveDem$Id & SveDem$DIAGNOSIS_BR[match(o_amoris$sampleID, SveDem$Id)] == 7, 1, 0) #7
o_amoris$S_uns <- ifelse(o_amoris$sampleID %in% SveDem$Id & SveDem$DIAGNOSIS_BR[match(o_amoris$sampleID, SveDem$Id)] == 8, 1, 0) #8
o_amoris$S_oth <- ifelse(o_amoris$sampleID %in% SveDem$Id & SveDem$DIAGNOSIS_BR[match(o_amoris$sampleID, SveDem$Id)] == 9, 1, 0) #9

# Create the new column by matching sampleID from o_amoris to Id in SveDem
o_amoris$S_INDATUM <- SveDem$DIAGNOSIS_DATE_BR[match(o_amoris$sampleID, SveDem$Id)]

# Codes for the ones not in SveDem
alzheimers_codes <- c(
  "G308", "G309", "G301", "F009", "F002", "G300", "F001", "F000",
  "290,1", "304", "290", "290A", "F00", "305", "290B", "G30", "311A"
)

vascular_codes <- c(
  "293", "290E", "F01", "293,1", "F019", "F012", "F018",
  "F013", "F011", "F010", "F0180", "F0183"
)

other_codes <- c(
  "F039", "F23", "F020", "F024", "F028", "F022", "F03-p", "F021", "F023", "F03-P",
  "290,0", "293,9", "293,2", "293,5", "293,3", "293,4", "F0013", "F0010",
  "306", "290X", "F02", "290W", "F03", "294B", "G311",
  "311B", "G318A", "311C", "F051", "311X"
)

all_codes <- unique(c(alzheimers_codes, vascular_codes, other_codes))

#Then we make an overall category
o_amoris$ADRD <- ifelse(
  (o_amoris$Dementia != "" & !is.na(o_amoris$Dementia)) |
    (o_amoris$ATC != "" & !is.na(o_amoris$ATC)) |
    (o_amoris$S_ADRD == 1),
  1,
  0
)

# Prioritize SveDem info, fallback to Dementia codes
o_amoris$Alzheimers <- ifelse(
  o_amoris$S_l_alz == 1 | o_amoris$S_e_alz == 1 | o_amoris$S_alz_vas == 1,
  1,
  ifelse(o_amoris$Dementia %in% alzheimers_codes, 1, 0)
)

o_amoris$Vascular <- ifelse(
  o_amoris$S_vas == 1,
  1,
  ifelse(o_amoris$Dementia %in% vascular_codes, 1, 0)
)

o_amoris$Other <- ifelse(
  o_amoris$S_oth == 1 | o_amoris$S_uns == 1 | o_amoris$S_par == 1 | o_amoris$S_fro == 1 | o_amoris$S_lew == 1,
  1,
  ifelse(o_amoris$Dementia %in% other_codes, 1, 0)
)

# Adds the people with no dementia diagnosis but ATC code to alzheimers, the people with dementia drugs have alzheimers
o_amoris$Alzheimers <- ifelse(o_amoris$ATC != "" & o_amoris$Dementia == "" & o_amoris$S_ADRD == "", 1, o_amoris$Alzheimers)
```

```{r}
  as.numeric(as.character(o_amoris$DispInk_quartile)),  # Convert factor to numeric
  ifelse(

) / 365.25
```

```{r}
  dplyr::left_join(o_amoris %>%
              dplyr::select(AgeAtFirstDate, AgeAtLastDate, income_bins, NewUtbNiva, birthcohort, ADRD, Alzheimers, Vascular, Other, sampleID), by = "sampleID")
```

## 1.5 Create the baseline for the longitudinal subset
```{r}
results_df <- results_dt %>%
  group_by(sampleID) %>%
  slice_min(order_by = age, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## 1.6 Beta function
```{r}
calc_standardized_beta <- function(model, data, covariate) {
    beta <- coef(model)[covariate]
    sd_covariate <- sd(data[[covariate]], na.rm = TRUE)
    std_beta <- beta * sd_covariate
    return(std_beta)
}
```

# 2.0 Time to event analysis: association at baseline for the longitudinal subset

## 2.1 ADRD
```{r}
# BA measures to be tested
BA_measures <- c("kdm_advance_sd", "phenoage_advance_sd")

# Correct the initialization of HR_BA data frame
HR_BA <- data.frame(
  BA = rep(BA_measures, each = 2),  # Repeat each BA measure twice
  outcome = rep("ADRD", times = length(BA_measures) * 2),
  model = rep(c("Sex-adjusted model", "Multivariable model"), times = length(BA_measures)),
  beta = NA, se = NA, HR = NA, CI_lower = NA, CI_upper = NA, p = NA, p_PH_BA = NA, global_p_PH_BA = NA,
  concordance = NA, N = NA, events = NA , std_beta = NA  # Add a column for the concordance index
)

for (j in 1:length(BA_measures)) {
  # Sex-adjusted model
  fit_gender <- coxph(as.formula(paste("Surv(AgeAtFirstDate, AgeAtLastDate, ADRD) ~", BA_measures[j], "+ gender")), data = results_df)
  coef_gender <- summary(fit_gender)
  row_index_gender <- (j * 2) - 1
  std_beta_gender <- calc_standardized_beta(fit_gender, results_df, BA_measures[j])
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, c(4, 5, 9, 12)] <- c(coef_gender$coefficients[1, c(1, 3, 5)], coef_gender$concordance[1])
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, c("HR", "CI_lower", "CI_upper")] <- coef_gender$conf.int[1, c(1, 3, 4)]
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, 10] <- cox.zph(fit_gender)$table[1, 3]
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, 11] <- cox.zph(fit_gender)$table["GLOBAL", "p"]
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, "N"] <- coef_gender$n
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, "std_beta"] <- std_beta_gender
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, "events"] <- fit_gender$nevent

  # Multivariable model
  fit_multivariable <- coxph(as.formula(paste("Surv(AgeAtFirstDate, AgeAtLastDate, ADRD) ~", BA_measures[j], "+ gender + income_bins + NewUtbNiva ")), data = results_df) #birthcohort
  coef_multivariable <- summary(fit_multivariable)
  row_index_multivariable <- j * 2
  std_beta_multivariable <- calc_standardized_beta(fit_multivariable, results_df, BA_measures[j])
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, c(4, 5, 9, 12)] <- c(coef_multivariable$coefficients[1, c(1, 3, 5)], coef_multivariable$concordance[1])
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, c("HR", "CI_lower", "CI_upper")] <- coef_multivariable$conf.int[1, c(1, 3, 4)]
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, 10] <- cox.zph(fit_multivariable)$table[1, 3]
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, 11] <- cox.zph(fit_multivariable)$table["GLOBAL", "p"]
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, "N"] <- coef_multivariable$n
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, "std_beta"] <- std_beta_multivariable
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, "events"] <- fit_multivariable$nevent
}

ADRD_results <- HR_BA

# Print the modified HR_BA_adrd data frame
print(HR_BA)
```

```{r}
  row_index_gender <- (j * 2) - 1
  std_beta_gender <- calc_standardized_beta(fit_gender, results_df, BA_measures[j])
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, c(4, 5, 9, 12)] <- c(coef_gender$coefficients[1, c(1, 3, 5)], coef_gender$concordance[1])
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, c("HR", "CI_lower", "CI_upper")] <- coef_gender$conf.int[1, c(1, 3, 4)]
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, 10] <- cox.zph(fit_gender)$table[1, 3]
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, 11] <- cox.zph(fit_gender)$table["GLOBAL", "p"]
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, "N"] <- coef_gender$n
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, "std_beta"] <- std_beta_gender
  HR_BA[row_index_gender, "events"] <- fit_gender$nevent

  # Multivariable model
  fit_multivariable <- coxph(as.formula(paste("Surv(AgeAtFirstDate, AgeAtLastDate, Vascular) ~", BA_measures[j], "+ gender + income_bins + NewUtbNiva")), data = results_df)
  coef_multivariable <- summary(fit_multivariable)
  row_index_multivariable <- j * 2
  std_beta_multivariable <- calc_standardized_beta(fit_multivariable, results_df, BA_measures[j])
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, c(4, 5, 9, 12)] <- c(coef_multivariable$coefficients[1, c(1, 3, 5)], coef_multivariable$concordance[1])
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, c("HR", "CI_lower", "CI_upper")] <- coef_multivariable$conf.int[1, c(1, 3, 4)]
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, 10] <- cox.zph(fit_multivariable)$table[1, 3]
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, 11] <- cox.zph(fit_multivariable)$table["GLOBAL", "p"]
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, "N"] <- coef_multivariable$n
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, "std_beta"] <- std_beta_multivariable
  HR_BA[row_index_multivariable, "events"] <- fit_multivariable$nevent
}

Vasc_results <- HR_BA

# Print the modified HR_BA_adrd data frame
print(HR_BA)
```

# 3.0 Rate of change or intercept?

```{r}
# optional sensitivity analysis for out longitudinal set
# We have filtered out individuals who got ADRD at baseline already
# But people, although not many can still get it before their last measurement
# We want to count these individuals and filter them out as a sensitivity analysis
# we will for each individual check the AgeAtLastDate at their final row (so all rows need to be sorted first individual and then according to AgeAtFirstDate) against their AgeAtFirstDate for their current row
# Arrange by individual, then by age at measurement
results_dt_filt <- results_dt %>%
  arrange(sampleID, age)

n_ids_before <- n_distinct(results_dt_filt$sampleID)
n_rows_before <- nrow(results_dt_filt)

# How many rows are actually post-diagnosis (age measured after ADRD dx)?
n_rows_post_dx <- results_dt_filt %>%
  filter(ADRD == 1 & age > AgeAtLastDate) %>%
  nrow()

# How many distinct individuals have at least one such row?
ids_with_post_dx_measurement <- results_dt_filt %>%
  filter(ADRD == 1 & age > AgeAtLastDate) %>%
  distinct(sampleID) %>%
  pull(sampleID)

# Drop rows measured after the ADRD diagnosis age
results_dt_filt <- results_dt_filt %>%
  filter(!(ADRD == 1 & age > AgeAtLastDate))

# Re-apply the >=3 measurements requirement now that some rows are gone
id_counts_filt <- table(results_dt_filt$sampleID)
keep_ids_filt <- names(id_counts_filt[id_counts_filt >= 3])

results_dt_filt <- results_dt_filt %>%
  filter(sampleID %in% keep_ids_filt)

n_ids_after <- n_distinct(results_dt_filt$sampleID)

# Summary counts
cat("Individuals before filtering:              ", n_ids_before, "\n")
cat("Rows removed (post-diagnosis measurements): ", n_rows_post_dx, "\n")
cat("Individuals with >=1 post-dx measurement:   ", length(ids_with_post_dx_measurement), "\n")
cat("Individuals dropped entirely (<3 pre-dx obs):", n_ids_before - n_ids_after, "\n")
cat("Individuals remaining after filtering:      ", n_ids_after, "\n")
```

## 3.1 Making slopes (PhenoAge)
```{r}
library(data.table)

dt <- as.data.table(results_dt_filt)

# Compute per-individual slope and intercept with age centered at first measurement
slopes_dt <- dt[, if (.N >= 3) {
  age0 <- min(age, na.rm = TRUE)  # baseline CA
  model <- lm(phenoage_advance_sd ~ I(age - age0))
  .(slope = coef(model)[2], intercept = coef(model)[1])
}, by = sampleID]

# Merge back slope/intercept to all rows for eligible sampleIDs
results_phe <- merge(dt, slopes_dt, by = "sampleID", all.x = FALSE, all.y = TRUE)
```

## 3.3 Deduplicated rows

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# --- PhenoAge ---

results_phe_1row <- results_phe %>%
  distinct(sampleID, .keep_all = TRUE)

    " | rows after dedup:", nrow(results_phe_1row), "\n")
```

## 3.4 Sensitivity: robustness to removing one random measurement per individual

Per discussion with the biostatistician, individual slopes estimated from
few repeated measurements (mean 4.35 per person) may be sensitive to which
measurements happen to be available. As a robustness check, we randomly
remove one measurement per individual, re-estimate person-specific slopes
and intercepts on the remaining measurements, and refit the Cox models.
This is repeated twice (two independent random removals) for both PhenoAge
and KDM, so that the resulting HR table (Table 9) is produced twice for
comparison against the original estimates.

### 3.4.1 PhenoAge, random drop run 1
```{r}
set.seed(101)

# Randomly drop exactly one measurement row per individual
results_dt_drop1 <- results_dt_filt %>%
  group_by(sampleID) %>%
  filter(row_number() != sample(row_number(), 1)) %>%
  ungroup()

dt <- as.data.table(results_dt_drop1)

# Re-estimate slope/intercept per person on the remaining measurements
# (everyone had >=3 before dropping one, so >=2 remain)
slopes_dt <- dt[, if (.N >= 2) {
  age0 <- min(age, na.rm = TRUE)
  model <- lm(phenoage_advance_sd ~ I(age - age0))
  .(slope = coef(model)[2], intercept = coef(model)[1])
}, by = sampleID]

results_phe_drop1 <- merge(dt, slopes_dt, by = "sampleID", all.x = FALSE, all.y = TRUE) %>%
  distinct(sampleID, .keep_all = TRUE)

slope_phe_drop1 <- coxph(as.formula(paste("Surv(AgeAtFirstDate, AgeAtLastDate, ADRD) ~", "slope + intercept", "+ gender")), data = results_phe_drop1)
slope_phe_drop1_sum <- summary(slope_phe_drop1)
slope_phe_drop1_sum
```

## 3.5 Table 9 (random-drop sensitivity), produced twice for comparison
```{r}
extract_hr_table <- function(model_summary, label) {
  data.frame(
    Model    = label,
    term     = rownames(model_summary$coefficients),
    HR       = model_summary$conf.int[, "exp(coef)"],
    CI_lower = model_summary$conf.int[, "lower .95"],
    CI_upper = model_summary$conf.int[, "upper .95"],
    p        = model_summary$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"],
    n        = model_summary$n,
    events   = model_summary$nevent
  )
}

table9_sensitivity <- rbind(
  extract_hr_table(slope_phe_1row_sum, "PhenoAge - original (no drop)"),
  extract_hr_table(slope_phe_drop1_sum, "PhenoAge - random drop, run 1"),
  extract_hr_table(slope_phe_drop2_sum, "PhenoAge - random drop, run 2"),
  extract_hr_table(slope_kdm_1row_sum, "KDM - original (no drop)"),
  extract_hr_table(slope_kdm_drop1_sum, "KDM - random drop, run 1"),
  extract_hr_table(slope_kdm_drop2_sum, "KDM - random drop, run 2")
)

print(table9_sensitivity)

write.table(table9_sensitivity, out_path("table9_random_drop_sensitivity_RMA.csv"), sep = ";",
            dec = ",", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, fileEncoding = "Latin1")
```

# 3.6 Delayed entry at the last measurement used for the slope (Reviewer 3)

Inclusion requires >=3 pre-diagnosis measurements, but follow-up in 3.3 starts
at the first measurement, so everyone is ADRD-free by construction until their
3rd (and later) measurement. Here slope and intercept are unchanged (same
estimates as 3.1/3.2, intercept still centred at the first measurement), but
each person enters the risk set at the age of the last measurement used to
estimate them. Age is the timescale, so this is left truncation:
Surv(AgeAtEntry, AgeAtLastDate, ADRD).

## 3.6.1 Entry age per individual
```{r}
# results_dt_filt holds exactly the measurements used in 3.1/3.2
# (post-diagnosis rows removed, >=3 rows per person)
entry_dt <- results_dt_filt %>%
  group_by(sampleID) %>%
  summarise(
    AgeAtFirstMeas = min(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    AgeAtEntry     = max(age, na.rm = TRUE),  # last measurement used for slope
    n_meas         = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

results_phe_de <- results_phe_1row %>% left_join(entry_dt, by = "sampleID")
results_kdm_de <- results_kdm_1row %>% left_join(entry_dt, by = "sampleID")
```

## 3.6.2 Who is lost by delaying entry?
```{r}
# Individuals whose exit (ADRD dx, death, emigration, end of follow-up) is at or
# before their last measurement contribute no person-time after entry
delayed_entry_summary <- function(d, label) {
  lost <- !is.na(d$AgeAtLastDate) & d$AgeAtLastDate <= d$AgeAtEntry
  cat(label, "\n")
  cat("  Individuals:                              ", nrow(d), "\n")
  cat("  ADRD events (entry at first measurement): ", sum(d$ADRD == 1, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  cat("  Exit at/before entry (excluded):          ", sum(lost), "\n")
  cat("    of which ADRD events:                   ", sum(lost & d$ADRD == 1, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
  cat("  Measurement window, first -> last measurement (years):\n")
  print(summary(d$AgeAtEntry - d$AgeAtFirstMeas))
  cat("  Follow-up after entry (years), retained individuals:\n")
  print(summary((d$AgeAtLastDate - d$AgeAtEntry)[!lost]))
  cat("  Follow-up from first measurement (years), original model:\n")
  print(summary(d$AgeAtLastDate - d$AgeAtFirstDate))
}

delayed_entry_summary(results_phe_de, "PhenoAge")
delayed_entry_summary(results_kdm_de, "KDM")

# Keep individuals with person-time after entry (coxph requires stop > start)
results_phe_de <- results_phe_de %>% filter(AgeAtLastDate > AgeAtEntry)
results_kdm_de <- results_kdm_de %>% filter(AgeAtLastDate > AgeAtEntry)
```

```{r}
table_delayed_entry <- rbind(
  extract_hr_table(slope_phe_1row_sum, "PhenoAge - entry at first measurement (original)"),
  extract_hr_table(slope_phe_de_sum,   "PhenoAge - entry at last measurement (delayed entry)"),
  extract_hr_table(slope_kdm_1row_sum, "KDM - entry at first measurement (original)"),
  extract_hr_table(slope_kdm_de_sum,   "KDM - entry at last measurement (delayed entry)")
)
```

# 3.7 Random-drop sensitivity with delayed entry

Same random removals as 3.4 (same seeds, same results_dt_filt, so the same
measurement is dropped per person), but entry is now the age of the last
measurement remaining after the drop, i.e. the last one used for the slope.
If the dropped measurement was the last one, entry moves to the one before.

## 3.7.1 Helper
```{r}
fit_drop_delayed_entry <- function(seed, ba_var, label) {
  set.seed(seed)

  # Randomly drop exactly one measurement row per individual (as in 3.4)
  d_drop <- results_dt_filt %>%
    group_by(sampleID) %>%
    filter(row_number() != sample(row_number(), 1)) %>%
    ungroup()

  dt <- as.data.table(d_drop)
  dt$ba_y <- dt[[ba_var]]

  # Slope/intercept on remaining measurements, plus entry age = last one used
  slopes_dt <- dt[, if (.N >= 2) {
    age0 <- min(age, na.rm = TRUE)
    model <- lm(ba_y ~ I(age - age0))
    .(slope = coef(model)[2], intercept = coef(model)[1],
      AgeAtEntry = max(age, na.rm = TRUE))
  }, by = sampleID]

  d1 <- merge(dt, slopes_dt, by = "sampleID", all.x = FALSE, all.y = TRUE) %>%
    distinct(sampleID, .keep_all = TRUE)

  lost <- !is.na(d1$AgeAtLastDate) & d1$AgeAtLastDate <= d1$AgeAtEntry
  counts <- data.frame(
    Model           = label,
    n_before        = nrow(d1),
    events_before   = sum(d1$ADRD == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_excluded      = sum(lost),
    events_excluded = sum(lost & d1$ADRD == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

  d1 <- d1 %>% filter(AgeAtLastDate > AgeAtEntry)

  fit <- coxph(Surv(AgeAtEntry, AgeAtLastDate, ADRD) ~ slope + intercept + gender,
               data = d1)

  list(sum = summary(fit), counts = counts, fit = fit, data = d1)
}
```

## 3.7.2 Runs (PhenoAge and KDM, seeds 101 and 202)
```{r}
phe_drop1_de <- fit_drop_delayed_entry(101, "phenoage_advance_sd", "PhenoAge - random drop, run 1 (delayed entry)")
phe_drop2_de <- fit_drop_delayed_entry(202, "phenoage_advance_sd", "PhenoAge - random drop, run 2 (delayed entry)")

kdm_drop2_de <- fit_drop_delayed_entry(202, "kdm_advance_sd",      "KDM - random drop, run 2 (delayed entry)")

kdm_drop1_de$sum
kdm_drop2_de$sum

# Individuals/events lost because exit was at or before entry

                        kdm_drop1_de$counts, kdm_drop2_de$counts)
print(drop_de_counts)
```

# 3.8 Person-mean centering (Reviewer 3)

With age centred at the first measurement, the estimation errors of each
person's intercept and slope are correlated. Centring age at the person's mean
measurement age makes them uncorrelated. The OLS slope is identical under both
centrings; only the intercept changes, to the level at the person's mean age
(= the person's mean BA advance). Fitted with both entry definitions.

## 3.8.1 Slopes and intercepts with person-mean centering
```{r}
make_pm_slopes <- function(ba_var) {
  dt <- as.data.table(results_dt_filt)
  dt$ba_y <- dt[[ba_var]]

  slopes_dt <- dt[, if (.N >= 3) {
    age_bar <- mean(age[!is.na(ba_y)])  # person-mean age over rows used in lm
    model <- lm(ba_y ~ I(age - age_bar))
    .(slope = coef(model)[2], intercept = coef(model)[1])
  }, by = sampleID]

  merge(dt, slopes_dt, by = "sampleID", all.x = FALSE, all.y = TRUE) %>%
    distinct(sampleID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    left_join(entry_dt, by = "sampleID")
}

results_phe_pm <- make_pm_slopes("phenoage_advance_sd")
results_kdm_pm <- make_pm_slopes("kdm_advance_sd")

# Slopes should be identical to 3.1/3.2; intercepts differ
cat("PhenoAge max |slope difference| vs first-measurement centering:",
    max(abs(results_phe_pm$slope -
              results_phe_1row$slope[match(results_phe_pm$sampleID, results_phe_1row$sampleID)]),
        na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("KDM max |slope difference| vs first-measurement centering:     ",
    max(abs(results_kdm_pm$slope -
              results_kdm_1row$slope[match(results_kdm_pm$sampleID, results_kdm_1row$sampleID)]),
        na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

# Between-person correlation of intercept and slope under each centering
cat("Correlation intercept-slope, PhenoAge: first-meas =",
    round(cor(results_phe_1row$intercept, results_phe_1row$slope, use = "complete.obs"), 3),
    "| person-mean =",
    round(cor(results_phe_pm$intercept, results_phe_pm$slope, use = "complete.obs"), 3), "\n")
cat("Correlation intercept-slope, KDM:      first-meas =",
    round(cor(results_kdm_1row$intercept, results_kdm_1row$slope, use = "complete.obs"), 3),
    "| person-mean =",
    round(cor(results_kdm_pm$intercept, results_kdm_pm$slope, use = "complete.obs"), 3), "\n")
```

# 3.9 Slope scaling check: main vs drop-one models (Reviewer 3)

Reviewer 3 noted the slope SE is ~0.016-0.019 in the main models but ~0.002-0.004
in the drop-one models. Hypothesis: after dropping a measurement many people
have only 2 points left, often close in time, giving extreme slopes. A larger
SD of the slope covariate shrinks the per-unit SE without any real gain in
precision. Check the slope distribution, then compare HRs per SD.

## 3.9.1 Slope distribution and measurement span
```{r}
slope_dist <- function(d, label) {
  data.frame(
    Model          = label,
    n              = sum(!is.na(d$slope)),
    sd_slope       = sd(d$slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    p01_slope      = quantile(d$slope, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_slope   = median(d$slope, na.rm = TRUE),
    p99_slope      = quantile(d$slope, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_intercept   = sd(d$intercept, na.rm = TRUE),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

table_slope_dist <- rbind(
  slope_dist(results_phe_1row,       "PhenoAge - main"),
  slope_dist(results_phe_drop1,      "PhenoAge - drop run 1"),
  slope_dist(results_phe_drop2,      "PhenoAge - drop run 2"),
  slope_dist(results_kdm_1row,       "KDM - main"),
  slope_dist(results_kdm_drop1,      "KDM - drop run 1"),
  slope_dist(results_kdm_drop2,      "KDM - drop run 2")
)
print(table_slope_dist)

# Span of the measurements left after the drop (years), and how many have 2 points
span_after_drop <- function(seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  results_dt_filt %>%
    group_by(sampleID) %>%
    filter(row_number() != sample(row_number(), 1)) %>%
    summarise(n_left = n(), span = max(age) - min(age), .groups = "drop")
}
for (s in c(101, 202)) {
  sp <- span_after_drop(s)
  cat("Seed", s, "- individuals with only 2 measurements left:", sum(sp$n_left == 2), "\n")
  cat("  Span (years) among those with 2 left:\n"); print(summary(sp$span[sp$n_left == 2]))
}
cat("Span (years) in main data:\n")
print(summary(entry_dt$AgeAtEntry - entry_dt$AgeAtFirstMeas))
```

## 3.9.2 HRs per SD of slope and intercept
```{r}
# HR per SD = exp(beta * SD), SD taken in the sample the model was fitted on
per_sd_rows <- function(fit, data, label) {
  s  <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  cc <- data[complete.cases(data[, c("slope", "intercept", "gender", "ADRD", "AgeAtLastDate")]), ]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("slope", "intercept"), function(v) {
    sdv <- sd(cc[[v]])
    b   <- s[v, "coef"]
    se  <- s[v, "se(coef)"]
    data.frame(
      Model     = label,
      term      = v,
      SD        = sdv,
      beta      = b,
      se        = se,
      HR_per_SD = exp(b * sdv),
      CI_lower  = exp((b - 1.96 * se) * sdv),
      CI_upper  = exp((b + 1.96 * se) * sdv),
      p         = s[v, "Pr(>|z|)"],
      row.names = NULL
    )
  }))
}

table_per_sd <- rbind(
  per_sd_rows(slope_phe_1row,      results_phe_1row,      "PhenoAge - main, entry first meas"),
  per_sd_rows(slope_phe_drop1,     results_phe_drop1,     "PhenoAge - drop run 1, entry first meas"),
  per_sd_rows(slope_phe_drop2,     results_phe_drop2,     "PhenoAge - drop run 2, entry first meas"),
  per_sd_rows(slope_phe_de,        results_phe_de,        "PhenoAge - main, delayed entry"),
  per_sd_rows(phe_drop1_de$fit,    phe_drop1_de$data,     "PhenoAge - drop run 1, delayed entry"),
  per_sd_rows(phe_drop2_de$fit,    phe_drop2_de$data,     "PhenoAge - drop run 2, delayed entry"),
  per_sd_rows(slope_phe_pm,        results_phe_pm,        "PhenoAge - person-mean, entry first meas"),
  per_sd_rows(slope_phe_pm_de,     results_phe_pm_de,     "PhenoAge - person-mean, delayed entry"),
  per_sd_rows(slope_kdm_1row,      results_kdm_1row,      "KDM - main, entry first meas"),
  per_sd_rows(slope_kdm_drop1,     results_kdm_drop1,     "KDM - drop run 1, entry first meas"),
  per_sd_rows(slope_kdm_drop2,     results_kdm_drop2,     "KDM - drop run 2, entry first meas"),
  per_sd_rows(slope_kdm_de,        results_kdm_de,        "KDM - main, delayed entry"),
  per_sd_rows(kdm_drop1_de$fit,    kdm_drop1_de$data,     "KDM - drop run 1, delayed entry"),
  per_sd_rows(kdm_drop2_de$fit,    kdm_drop2_de$data,     "KDM - drop run 2, delayed entry"),
  per_sd_rows(slope_kdm_pm,        results_kdm_pm,        "KDM - person-mean, entry first meas"),
  per_sd_rows(slope_kdm_pm_de,     results_kdm_pm_de,     "KDM - person-mean, delayed entry")
```

# 3.10 Baseline Cox in the longitudinal subset with delayed entry (Supplementary Figs. 29-30)

Same models as section 2 (baseline KDM/PhenoAge age gap at the first
measurement; sex-adjusted and multivariable; ADRD and subtypes), but in the
same analytic set as the slope/intercept models: post-diagnosis measurements
removed, >=3 pre-diagnosis measurements (results_dt_filt), and delayed entry
at the age of the last measurement (AgeAtEntry from 3.6.1).

## 3.10.1 Analytic set
```{r}
results_df_de <- results_dt_filt %>%
  group_by(sampleID) %>%
  slice_min(order_by = age, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%   # exposure at first measurement
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(entry_dt %>% dplyr::select(sampleID, AgeAtEntry), by = "sampleID")

cat("Individuals in longitudinal subset (one row each):", nrow(results_df_de), "\n")

    sum(results_df_de$AgeAtLastDate <= results_df_de$AgeAtEntry, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
```

## 3.10.2 Models (same layout as combined_results in 2.5)
```{r}
BA_measures <- c("kdm_advance_sd", "phenoage_advance_sd")
outcomes    <- c("Alzheimers", "ADRD", "Other", "Vascular")  # same order as 2.5

fit_baseline_de <- function(outcome) {
  HR_BA <- data.frame(
    BA = rep(BA_measures, each = 2),
    outcome = rep(outcome, times = length(BA_measures) * 2),
    model = rep(c("Sex-adjusted model", "Multivariable model"), times = length(BA_measures)),
    beta = NA, se = NA, HR = NA, CI_lower = NA, CI_upper = NA, p = NA, p_PH_BA = NA, global_p_PH_BA = NA,
    concordance = NA, N = NA, events = NA, std_beta = NA
  )
  covs <- c("+ gender", "+ gender + income_bins + NewUtbNiva")
  for (j in seq_along(BA_measures)) {
    for (k in 1:2) {
      fit <- coxph(as.formula(paste0("Surv(AgeAtEntry, AgeAtLastDate, ", outcome, ") ~ ",
                                     BA_measures[j], " ", covs[k])), data = results_df_de)
      s <- summary(fit)
      i <- (j - 1) * 2 + k
      HR_BA[i, c(4, 5, 9, 12)] <- c(s$coefficients[1, c(1, 3, 5)], s$concordance[1])
      HR_BA[i, c("HR", "CI_lower", "CI_upper")] <- s$conf.int[1, c(1, 3, 4)]
      HR_BA[i, 10] <- cox.zph(fit)$table[1, 3]
      HR_BA[i, 11] <- cox.zph(fit)$table["GLOBAL", "p"]
      HR_BA[i, "N"] <- s$n
      HR_BA[i, "events"] <- fit$nevent
      HR_BA[i, "std_beta"] <- calc_standardized_beta(fit, results_df_de, BA_measures[j])
    }
  }
  HR_BA
}

combined_results_de <- do.call(rbind, lapply(outcomes, fit_baseline_de))
print(combined_results_de)

write.table(combined_results_de, out_path("combined_results_ADRD_Baseline_forL_delayed_entry.csv"), sep = ";",
            dec = ",", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, fileEncoding = "Latin1")
```
